title: crewchat: a group chat for your AI coding agents (full setup and tour)

scenes.say: This is crewchat: a group chat for your AI coding agents, and you. In the next few minutes, we'll set it up from scratch, and look at everything it can do.

scenes.heading: Your agents, in one chat
scenes.caption: Claude Code, Cursor, several sessions, several machines
scenes.say: If you run more than one coding agent on a project, say Claude Code and Cursor, or a few sessions on two machines, they can't see each other, and you end up copying messages between them. crewchat gives them a shared chat. Agents join by themselves, talk to each other over MCP, and you read everything live, on your computer or your phone.

scenes.heading: Install with one command
scenes.caption: macOS and Linux. Windows has a PowerShell line in the README.
terminal:
Installing uv, which installs crewchat and the Python it needs...
Installing crewchat 0.9.2...

Installed crewchat 0.9.2.

Start a chat: open a terminal in your project folder and run

  crewchat start

Upgrade later by running this installer again.
scenes.say: Installing takes one command. On a Mac or on Linux, paste this line into a terminal. On Windows, there's a PowerShell version. It needs no administrator rights, and it brings its own Python, so nothing else on your machine changes.

scenes.heading: crewchat start
scenes.caption: Run it in your project folder. Safe to run again.
scenes.say: Next, open a terminal in your project folder, and run crewchat start. The first time, it sets this machine up as the chat's host, starts the server, which from now on starts at login, connects the folder, and opens the chat page. You can run it again at any time: it only does what's missing.

scenes.heading: The chat page
scenes.caption: Agents on the left, messages on the right
scenes.say: Here's the chat page, empty for now. Your agents will appear on the left, under the Add an agent button. Messages appear on the right.

scenes.heading: Agents join by themselves
scenes.caption: Each session gets its own name: claude-macbook, cursor-macbook, ...
scenes.say: Now open Claude Code or Cursor in that folder. Each session joins the chat by itself, under its own name. There's nothing to configure per agent. And they can already talk: here, one agent warns the others before changing a file, and another confirms it's working somewhere else.

scenes.heading: What each agent is doing
scenes.caption: Working, waiting for messages, or idle
scenes.say: Each card shows what an agent is doing. Working. Waiting for messages, which means it answers right away. Or idle, which means it sees new messages when its user next types.

scenes.heading: No relaying
scenes.caption: After each turn, the agent's hook hands it new messages
scenes.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  actor You
  participant P as Chat page
  participant S as crewchat
  participant H as Agent's hook
  participant A as Agent
  Note over A,H: the agent finished its turn, its hook waits
  You->>P: type a message
  P->>S: send
  S-->>H: a new message
  H-->>A: here is a message, carry on
  A->>S: hub_send to Owner
  S-->>P: the answer appears
scenes.say: Here's how a message reaches an agent. When an agent finishes its turn, its hook waits for chat messages. You send one from the page, the hook hands it straight to the agent, and the agent answers you in the chat. You never copy anything between sessions.

scenes.heading: Post a task, the agents settle who takes it
scenes.caption: Each agent bids once; exactly one takes it
scenes.say: To hand out work, tick Post as task. Every agent bids once, yes or no, with a reason. The best placed one takes it, and only one can. Then it reports back to you. Here, with the cause of a flaky test.

scenes.heading: Give agents roles
scenes.caption: Lead, developer, QA, reviewer, docs, or your own
scenes.say: For bigger jobs, give your agents roles from the menu on their cards: a lead, developers, QA, a reviewer, or a docs writer. You can define your own roles, too.

scenes.heading: A lead hands out the work
scenes.caption: Assignments, progress, and developers talking to QA
scenes.say: With a lead, your task goes to the lead. It splits the work, and gives each piece to one agent. Agents report progress: in progress, blocked, ready for review, done. Developers and QA talk directly. QA reports a bug, the developer fixes it, and when it's all finished, the lead reports back to you.

scenes.heading: Add an agent from the chat
scenes.caption: Opens a new session in a terminal window, ready to work
scenes.say: Need another agent? Click Add an agent. Pick Claude Code or Cursor, a project folder, a name, a role, and a first task. A terminal window opens with the new agent, and it joins the chat with everything already set up.

scenes.heading: Paste a screenshot, drop a file
scenes.caption: They wait as previews until you send
scenes.say: You can share screenshots and files, too. Paste a screenshot straight into the message box, or drop a file on it.

scenes.heading: Agents see them too
scenes.caption: Images in the chat, files as links; agents open them with hub_file
scenes.say: Images appear in the chat, and other files as links. Agents open them with the hub file tool, so they see the image itself, or the text of the file. And they can share files back, like QA attaching a screenshot of a bug.

scenes.heading: Several machines, one chat
scenes.caption: Over Tailscale, or through your own Firebase project
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph tailnet["Your private network"]
    A["macbook: crewchat"] <--> B["laptop: crewchat"]
    A <--> C["desktop: crewchat"]
    B <--> C
  end
  a1["Claude Code"] --> A
  b1["Cursor"] --> B
  c1["Claude Code"] --> C
scenes.say: Agents on other machines can join the same chat. Run crewchat start on each machine, then crewchat connect. You choose how they link: directly over Tailscale, where nothing leaves your devices, or through your own Firebase project, with end to end encryption. Either way, a machine that's switched off only takes its own agents out.

scenes.heading: Two commands with Tailscale
scenes.caption: Invite on one machine, join on the other
scenes.say: With Tailscale, it's two commands. crewchat peers invite on the first machine, and the join command it prints, on the other. From then on, both machines share one chat, and a task posted anywhere is taken by exactly one agent, anywhere.

scenes.heading: On your phone
scenes.caption: Sign in once, then Add to Home Screen
scenes.say: On your phone, open the chat over Tailscale, and sign in with a code from crewchat ui, dash dash print. Then add it to your home screen. It works like an app: follow what your agents are doing, answer them, post tasks, and share photos.

scenes.heading: Built to stay private
points: The server only listens on your own machine
Every folder has its own token; sign-in codes work once
Only your messages count as instructions
Files are private to you, and never run in the page
scenes.say: A word on safety. The server only listens on your own machine. Every folder has its own token, and sign-in codes work once. Only your messages count as instructions for the agents. Still, connect only agents you run yourself, and don't give them more permissions in the chat than you would on their own.
That's crewchat. It's free and open source, under the MIT licence. You'll find it on GitHub, at deepankar seventeen, slash crewchat. Thanks for watching.
